entries.title: I Samuel 2:1
segments:
My horn is exalted; the horn was an emblem of power: the Lord would cause her to triumph over all her foes. 
 
Whenever we receive new mercies, let who will be the instrument, we should feel that they come from God, and give him the praise.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:2
segments:
None besides thee; no other living and true God. 
 
  Rock; support, refuge, source of good.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:3
segments:
Actions are weighed; God perfectly understands their nature, character, and deserts. 
 
A conviction of the constant, all pervading presence of God tends to keep us from sin, excite us to duty, and make us humble, grateful, and better fitted for every good work.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:4
segments:
The mighty; who trust in their own strength. 
 
  They that stumbled; the feeble who trust in God.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:5
segments:
Ceased; ceased to be hungry, from the abundance that God gave them. 
 
  Borne seven; had many children.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:6
segments: Changes in the condition of individuals, families, and nations, though brought about by human instrumentality, are ordered by the Lord, and his agency in them should always be acknowledged.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:8
segments: The pillars of the earth are the Lord's; he made and sustains it, and he overrules and disposes of all its concerns.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:9
segments:
Keep the feet of his saints; preserve them. 
 
  By strength; of any created arm. 
 
However great the opposition of the wicked, the righteous shall finally overcome, and the temporary successes of the wicked will end in their final and everlasting defeat.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:10
segments: His king--his anointed; this is the first time the word Messiah, or the Anointed, is mentioned in the Bible.  It is applied to David and to Christ.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:11
segments: Ramah; the same as Ramathaim-sophim.

Minister unto the Lord; perform such services about the sanctuary as were suited to his age. 
 
God is greatly pleased when little children devote themselves to his service; and the smallest child who loves him has more true spiritual knowledge than the greatest and most learned man who neglects his service.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:12
segments: Sons of Eli; Hophni and Phinehas.

Sons of Belial; exceedingly wicked. 
 
  Knew not the Lord; on account of the wickedness of the priests. 
 
Men may be called priests, or ministers of religion, may conduct the forms of public worship, and have the best opportunities of knowing God, and yet hate him and be guilty of the most enormous wickedness.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:13
segments: Seething; boiling.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:14
segments: The priest took; this was robbing the offerer.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:15
segments: Sodden; boiled.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:16
segments: I will take it; this was an additional robbery.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:17
segments:
Men abhorred the offering of the Lord; on account of the wickedness of the priests. 
 
A covetous, self-indulgent, and licentious ministry is one of the greatest curses to the souls of men.  It leads multitudes to despise the ordinances of religion and sink into the darkness and pollution of infidelity.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:18
segments: A linen ephod; a garment like that which was worn by the priests.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:20
segments: The loan;

1Sa 1.28. 
 
A freewill offering to the Lord, even of that which is his, he receives with delight, and bestows upon the offerer an abundant reward.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:22
segments: When those who have the right and the power to put licentious men out of the ministry, neglect to do it, they become partakers in their sins, and will share their woes.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:24
segments: Ye make the Lord's people to transgress; by tempting them to sin.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:25
segments:
The judge shall judge him; if it were an offence of a man against his fellow-man, he might be punished according to the law; or by offering the appointed sacrifice, he might through faith in Christ be forgiven.  But this was a sin not only against men, but against God; it profaned the sacrifice which typified the sacrifice of Christ, and there remained no more sacrifice for sin, but a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation.  Such was probably the meaning of Eli, but he did not convey it with clearness and power to the minds of his profilgate sons.  Nor did he, as he should have done, act it out, by not only reproving them, but expelling them from their office and visiting them with condign punishment, as a warning to all of the guilt and danger of such wickedness.  He was a judge as well as a father, and should have been a terror to those evil-doers.  But he regarded his sons in this matter more than he did the honor of God. 
 
  Because; on account of their sins.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:26
segments:
In favor--with the Lord; God may have given him renewing grace in his infant years, in answer to the prayers of his mother. 
 
Parents who receive their children as the gift of God, and train them up in the way they should go, may hope that, through the renewing and sanctifying influences of the Holy Spirit, they will early devote themselves to the service of Christ, and continue in it to the end of life.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:27
segments: Appear unto the house of thy father; Eli descended from Aaron.
Great favors shown to any one lay him under great obligations to be faithful in the discharge of his appropriate duties, and will aggravate his guilt if he neglect them.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:29
segments:
Kick; dishonor, by profaning them or suffering them to be profaned. 
 
It is a great sin for parents to regard their children more than they do God, and the continued indulgence of this sin will bring upon them fearful punishment.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:30
segments: Walk before me;

For ever; to the end of the Jewish dispensation. 
 
  Lightly esteemed; rejected and punished.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:31
segments:
Cut off thine arm; cause his power and authority to cease. 
 
The sins of parents may deeply affect not only their children, but their distant posterity, even to the end of time and onward to eternity.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:32
segments: An enemy in my habitation; or, the affliction of the tabernacle, on account of the ark being taken by the Philistines, and other calamities.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:34
segments: A sign; an evidence that all which he had foretold would be accomplished.
When God makes declarations with regard to the future, he furnishes such evidence of the certainty of their accomplishment as ought to produce universal conviction.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:35
segments: A faithful priest; Zadok, a descendant not of Eli, but of Eleazar.

Build him a sure house; continue his posterity in the priesthood. 
 
  Mine anointed; the kings of David's line who would be anointed by him to their office, and from whom Christ would come. 
 
  For ever; as long as the kings of Israel should continue. 
 
The providence of God is a commentary on his word, and the more we see of the operations of the one, the more we shall see of the truth of the other.

entries.title: I Samuel 2:36
segments:
In thy house; of Eli's descendants. 
 
  Shall say; on account of their great poverty and degradation.
